title: Hermitian Dual Lattice With Conductor p
body_html:
Hermitian Dual Lattice With Conductor p

This is the foundation-layer notation node for the conductor-\(\mathfrak p\) convention on hermitian dual lattices. It should be used by both epipelagic and supercuspidal nodes instead of the older epipelagic_theta.hermitian_dual_lattice_conductor_p.

In this knowledge base, the fixed additive character \(\psi:F\to \mathbb C^\times\) has conductor \(\mathfrak p\): it is trivial on \(\mathfrak p\) and nontrivial on \(\mathfrak o\). With this normalization, the hermitian dual of an \(o_D\)-lattice \(L\subseteq V\) is \[ L^\#=\{v\in V:\langle v,L\rangle_V\subseteq \mathfrak p_D\}. \]

This is the convention used for self-dual lattice functions in the theta-correspondence nodes. Some sources write the same object as \(L^\ast\); this knowledge base uses \(L^\#\) for the hermitian dual lattice.

The alternative convention \[ \{v\in V:\langle v,L\rangle_V\subseteq \mathfrak o_D\} \] belongs to a different normalization, equivalently a different conductor convention or a shifted duality convention. It should not be silently identified with the conductor-\(\mathfrak p\) dual above.

For symplectic lattice-model objects, the \(\psi\)-annihilator of a lattice \(A\subseteq W\) is likewise conductor-dependent: \[ A^\perp=\{w\in W:\psi(\langle w,A\rangle_W)=1\}. \] Under the present conductor-\(\mathfrak p\) assumption this means \(\langle w,A\rangle_W\subseteq \mathfrak p\). This is a symplectic annihilator, not the hermitian dual lattice \(L^\#\), even though both use the same conductor normalization.
